messages.text:
Create two PRs:

- One (PR #71) that makes a SiW Barrel prototype with similar detail as #70



- One establishes a main page that shows the current baseline layout(s), directly accessible from the README.md



      This can be all in markdown, and lists the current layout candidate(s) and shows an r-z view of it. When clicked on it, it lists the main features but very concise, and links the relevant decisions and PRs into it:



At the moment, we have one baseline layout:

- Tracker (as described) and documented in the PR
- Solenoid with 3T (PR #64, unmerged)
- EM Calo: SiW prototype (PR #70, unmerged, and PR #71 to come)
- HCal rough outline (will follow)
- No FCal (yet)
- No MS + MS Magnet system (yet)



From now one, if something is approved and merged to a layout prototype, make sure the mainpage updates.

I’ll build the detailed Si–W barrel prototype on top of #70 and prepare a separate layout-page PR with an r–z view, concise features and links to the governing decisions and PRs. I’ll also record the rule that future merged layout updates must update that page.

I’ll use the repository’s specialist workflow for the barrel design, layout summary and independent validation. I’ll first bring #70 forward to the merged #69 baseline so the barrel PR stays focused. The layout page will distinguish merged prototypes, open proposals and systems still to be designed.

The local ACTS/Spack preflight reports changed setup and lockfile fingerprints. I’ll reverify the installed DD4hep/Geant4 runtime before using it for the prototype checks; no new dependencies are needed.

The barrel can use standard square sensors. I’m using roughly metre-long slabs with shorter end slabs, shared readout bays and explicit cooling, while retaining the existing envelope and 48 layers. A slab centred on z = 0 avoids a mechanical gap there; sector and sensor gaps will still be measured and reported.

The first packing check found an aligned service gap that would leave some η bands completely blind. I’m staggering adjacent layers by one board pitch, using two standard end-slab lengths, to avoid repeating those gaps through the full depth. The remaining sensor and sector cracks will stay visible in the coverage results.

[PR #71](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/71) is created as a draft while native validation runs. The implementation has 359,904 sensors and 92.1 million channels; its current budgets are about 299 tonnes and 188 kW under the stated cooling and continuous-power assumptions. The separate layout page and r–z drawing are also prepared.

The full barrel geometry passed native construction, mass, placement and readout checks, with zero overlaps at 10 nm across roughly 9.2 million placements. Independent reviews confirmed the packing and explained five boundary-ray differences using the silicon thickness. I’m strengthening two validator checks, then finishing the transport smoke tests and figures before marking #71 ready.

The strengthened geometry audit has passed, along with readout checks and three sparse Geant4 transport cases. I’m documenting those results in #71 and finishing the layout page, where each component will show its merged or proposed status.

The prototype’s mass budget is substantial: about 299 t, including 120 t of copper, with a 188 kW continuous-power hypothesis. #71 now makes those engineering questions explicit and shows the remaining sensor and service gaps alongside the material plots.

#71 is complete locally, with geometry, readout, material and sparse transport checks passing. The separate layout page links from the README to a clickable R–Z drawing and concise feature table. It also adds the requested maintenance rule for future approved and merged layout changes.

Both PRs are now open: [#71](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/71) contains the barrel prototype, and [#72](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/72) contains the layout main page. #71 is stacked on #70; #72 targets main independently. I’m checking the final hosted validation runs.

Both token-accounting builds have passed, and the layout page’s 16 source pins and 69 tracker input hashes check out. Full project CI is still running. Neither PR has merge conflicts; #71’s review notes keep the cooling, structural and acceptance questions open.

CI has passed the new calorimeter controls and shared geometry checks. It is now running the remaining tracker regressions. The layout page is pinned to the completed barrel revision, and both branches are clean locally.
The geometry and tracker checks have passed on both final revisions. CI is finishing the project-record and documentation checks; both PRs remain conflict-free and ready for review.

Created and pushed both PRs:

- [#71 — Detailed SiW barrel prototype](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/71): physical boards, supports, cooling, readout, mass/material checks and drawings. Native overlaps, 32 controls and sparse Geant4 checks pass. Merge #70 first.
- [#72 — Layout main page](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/72): README entry, clickable R–Z view, concise features and decision/PR links. Includes the future layout-update rule; targets main independently.

Both are ready, conflict-free and passed CI. Engineering and calorimeter-performance qualification remain open.
